name: Grant Writing Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in grant writing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in grant writing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When grant writing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Measure before optimizing any grant writing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Prefer the simplest grant writing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Keep grant writing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. State assumptions about grant writing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
6. Check that grant writing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
7. When grant writing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
8. Prefer explicit, readable grant writing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new grant writing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated grant writing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting grant writing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop grant writing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for grant writing, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
